subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make `pidsLimit: 1024` the default for existing unset Docker sandbox configs, and what opt-out/schema/docs/tests are required before shipping that security boundary change?
rationale: The mitigation is useful and source-reproducible, but default-on PID limiting changes upgrade behavior for existing sandbox users and needs owner approval of the security-versus-compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof cover fresh installs, upgrades, and explicit override semantics.

options.title: Keep default unset
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior and document operator-configured `pidsLimit` instead of changing existing deployments silently.

options.title: Use an opt-in strict profile
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved strict mode or profile if maintainers want the mitigation without changing unset deployments by default.

recommendation.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof cover fresh installs, upgrades, and explicit override semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the sandbox runtime/security surface to this team, and the unresolved question is a sandbox security boundary default.
